criteria.statement: A managed service that is healthy at the container level while its route returns HTTP 502 produces an open route outage distinctly classified as upstream_error, carrying the observed healthy container status.

A deployment whose post-deploy route canary fails is blocked and the route is rolled back through the routing backend's own compensation, with the failure classified as a canary gate failure rather than a provider failure.
An open route outage clears when the route returns, recording recovery and dropping the stale failure reason.

Checks are repo-configured and reproducible: hostname, protocol, path, expected status, expected body, TLS expiry window, public resolver, and internal split-DNS addresses all come from configuration, validated at startup when enabled.
Cloudflare edge and LAN/split-DNS perspectives are both checked where applicable, and a failure in either opens the outage.
TLS assertions verify a real chain for the canonical hostname and verification is never disabled, including when the dial address is pinned for a LAN check.
No secrets reach logs or durable evidence: response bodies and errors are bounded and sanitized, while body assertions match the raw body so redaction cannot change assertion semantics.
Route outage state and append-only failure lineage are operator-visible over the API alongside the container-level status, with no reliance on manual host commands.
A certificate nearing expiry is surfaced as a warning that never opens an outage and never blocks a deployment.

A health path that returns the same response as a deliberately bogus control path is reported as health_path_not_discriminating rather than route_ok, as a warning by default and as a blocking failure when require_discriminating_health_path is set.
The gate blocks and rolls back a route returning a status outside the expected range, confirming enforcement works for genuinely broken routes.
A gate run that verified nothing because the policy derived no targets is logged rather than silently reported as success.
Every route canary classification, perspective and transition defined in Go is admitted by the effective database CHECK constraints, enforced by a conformance test rather than by review.
